requirements.quote:
For the purpose of aggregating AS_PATH attributes of two routes,
      we model each AS as a tuple <type, value>, where "type" identifies
      a type of the path segment the AS belongs to (e.g., AS_SEQUENCE,
      AS_SET), and "value" is the AS number.  Two ASes are said to be
      the same if their corresponding <type, value> tuples are the same.
requirements.condition: If the implementation elects to use the optional Appendix F.6 aggregation procedure for two AS_PATH attributes
requirements.required_behavior: Model each AS by its path-segment type and AS number; regard ASes as the same only when both tuple components match.
requirements.why_checkable: Compare tuple equality using equal AS numbers in different segment types.

requirements.quote:
a) Identify the same ASes (as defined above) within each
            AS_PATH attribute that are in the same relative order within
            both AS_PATH attributes.  Two ASes, X and Y, are said to be
            in the same order if either:
Rekhter, et al.             Standards Track                    [Page 96]
RFC 4271                         BGP-4                      January 2006
              - X precedes Y in both AS_PATH attributes, or
              - Y precedes X in both AS_PATH attributes.
requirements.condition: If the implementation elects to use the optional Appendix F.6 aggregation procedure for two AS_PATH attributes; step (a), before constructing the aggregate
requirements.required_behavior: Identify matching AS tuples that retain the same relative order in both input AS_PATH attributes: X precedes Y in both or Y precedes X in both.
requirements.why_checkable: Matching subsequences can be checked against both input orders.

requirements.quote:
c) For each pair of adjacent tuples in the aggregated AS_PATH,
            if both tuples have the same type, merge them together if
            doing so will not cause a segment of a length greater than
            255 to be generated.
requirements.condition: If the implementation elects to use the optional Appendix F.6 aggregation procedure for two AS_PATH attributes; step (c), after constructing the aggregate, for each adjacent tuple pair of the same type whose merged segment length would be at most 255
requirements.required_behavior: Merge the adjacent tuples together.
requirements.why_checkable: Adjacent equal-type segments at and below the size limit exercise the merge rule.

requirements.quote:
c) For each pair of adjacent tuples in the aggregated AS_PATH,
            if both tuples have the same type, merge them together if

            255 to be generated.
requirements.condition: If the implementation elects to use the optional Appendix F.6 aggregation procedure for two AS_PATH attributes; step (c), merging an adjacent tuple pair would generate a segment longer than 255
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary cases of merged lengths 255 and 256 expose the size guard.

requirements.quote:
If, as a result of the above procedure, a given AS number appears
      more than once within the aggregated AS_PATH attribute, all but
      the last instance (rightmost occurrence) of that AS number should
      be removed from the aggregated AS_PATH attribute.
requirements.condition: If the implementation elects to use the optional Appendix F.6 aggregation procedure for two AS_PATH attributes; after the preceding procedure, an AS number occurs more than once in the aggregate
requirements.required_behavior: The implementation should remove all but the last (rightmost) occurrence of that AS number.
requirements.why_checkable: Duplicate AS numbers can be placed at several output positions to check recommended rightmost retention.

requirements.quote:
A BGP implementation MUST support the authentication mechanism
   specified in RFC 2385 [RFC2385].  The authentication provided by this
   mechanism could be done on a per-peer basis.
requirements.condition: For a BGP implementation
requirements.required_behavior: MUST support the authentication mechanism specified in RFC 2385.
requirements.why_checkable: Authentication support is an inspectable implementation capability; the chunk identifies the required mechanism.

requirements.quote:
BGP makes use of TCP for reliable transport of its traffic between
   peer routers.  To provide connection-oriented integrity and data
requirements.condition: For traffic between BGP peer routers
requirements.required_behavior: Use TCP for reliable transport.
requirements.why_checkable: The transport used for a BGP session is directly observable.

requirements.quote:
A compliant implementation must support this mechanism, and must
   allow a network administrator to activate it on a per-peer basis.
requirements.condition: For a compliant BGP implementation
requirements.required_behavior: Allow a network administrator to activate the RFC 2385 mechanism on a per-peer basis.
requirements.why_checkable: Configure authentication independently on two peers and inspect activation state.

requirements.quote:
RFC 2385 does not specify a means of managing (e.g., generating,
   distributing, and replacing) the keys used to compute the MAC.  RFC
   3562 [RFC3562] (an informational document) provides some guidance in
   this area, and provides rationale to support this guidance.  It notes
   that a distinct key should be used for communication with each
   protected peer.  If the same key is used for multiple peers, the
requirements.condition: For communication with protected peers; the cited key-management guidance is a recommendation
requirements.required_behavior: A distinct key should be used for each protected peer.
requirements.why_checkable: Peer authentication configuration can be compared for key reuse.

requirements.quote:
The keys used for MAC computation should be changed periodically, to
   minimize the impact of a key compromise or successful cryptanalytic
   attack.  RFC 3562 suggests a crypto period (the interval during which
   a key is employed) of, at most, 90 days.  More frequent key changes
   reduce the likelihood that replay attacks (as described above) will
   be feasible.  However, absent a standard mechanism for effecting such
   changes in a coordinated fashion between peers, one cannot assume
   that BGP-4 implementations complying with this RFC will support
   frequent key changes.
requirements.condition: For MAC key management; this is recommended practice, and the text does not require support for frequent coordinated key changes
requirements.required_behavior: MAC computation keys should be changed periodically.
requirements.why_checkable: Key replacement policy and key changes can be inspected without treating unspecified rotation frequency as mandatory.
